# BLO-40279: comments follow the GitHub-token mount off the shared CephFS volume

Change: [#2245](https://github.com/Blockcast/paperclip/pull/2245)

Files: `src/server/inherit-allowlist.ts`, `src/server/job-manifest.ts`, `src/server/k8s-client.ts`,
`src/server/job-manifest.test.ts` — comments only, no behaviour.

Both files document where `PAPERCLIP_GITHUB_TOKEN_FILE` points, and both named the old path
`/paperclip/.secrets/github-token/token`. That path was the defect
([BLO-40279](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/BLO/issues/BLO-40279)): the Secret was mounted
*underneath* the `/paperclip` CephFS volume, so a CSI re-mount stacked a fresh mount over it and
hid the Secret from every live container — `git` then refused fleet-wide because the wrapper
fails closed on an unreadable token, and 16 issues stranded on workspace validation in three
hours. The chart now mounts the token at `/etc/paperclip/secrets/github-token`, outside the
shared volume, where no remount of `/paperclip` can shadow it. These comments are updated to
match, because `job-manifest.ts`'s is the one that argues *why* the mount must not fail open —
an argument that reads as nonsense once it cites a path the chart no longer uses.

The PEN-3705 hazard argument in `job-manifest.ts`, `k8s-client.ts` and `job-manifest.test.ts` is
moved to the past tense rather than deleted. It was never just "the token goes missing": with the
mount nested under the PVC, losing it *uncovered* a mode-2775 fleet-writable directory at the same
path, so `PAPERCLIP_GITHUB_TOKEN_FILE` kept resolving and failing open handed every agent a
writable token path. That is why the `optional` passthrough is fail-closed. BLO-40279 removes the
reachability, not the rule — a future PVC-nested credential mount would reintroduce it, and the
passthrough is the thing that stops it being downgraded.

`k8s-client.ts`'s mention of the authbot key is corrected from `/run/authbot` to the chart's own
spelling `/var/run/authbot`. The resolved path really is `/run/authbot` — `/var/run` is a symlink
to `/run`, measured in-pod via `/proc/self/mountinfo` — but naming only the resolved form made
that mount look exempt from the `/var/run/*` note in `values.blockcast.yaml`, which it is not.
Nothing downstream read the old spelling; the claim it supports (that this mount was never
PVC-backed) is true of either.
